question: During which era was the Hazara Rama Temple, situated in Hampi, India, first established?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Early 15th century**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hazara Rama Temple** is located in **Hampi, Karnataka**, India, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The temple was established during the **Vijayanagara Empire** in the **early 15th century** under the reign of **King Devaraya I**.
 
• It is dedicated to **Lord Rama** and depicts scenes from the **Ramayana** on its walls.
 
• The temple is renowned for its **bas-relief carvings**, which are considered exemplary of the Vijayanagara architectural style.
 
• It served as a private temple for the royal family during the empire.
 
• The temple’s architecture reflects the **religious, cultural, and artistic significance** of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The Hazara Rama Temple is a **monumental representation** of the harmonious blend of devotion and art during that era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early 11th century**__

 __
 
• The **early 11th century** is marked by the **Chola dynasty** in Southern India, known for its grand temples such as the **Brihadeeswarar Temple**.
 
• While the Cholas were renowned for their architectural contributions, the **Vijayanagara Empire**, under which the Hazara Rama Temple was constructed, came much later.
 
 
 
• **Early 13th century**__
 __
 
• The **early 13th century** saw the rise of the Delhi Sultanate in northern India.
 
• It was an era of **, which was distinct from the Vijayanagara style prevalent in southern India.**
 
 ** **
 
• **Early 19th century**__ 
 
 
• **The early 19th century** was part of the colonial era in India under British rule.
 
• **Architectural works during this period focused more on British colonial designs** rather than indigenous styles.
